newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Ericsson invests 1 bln Skr in Kista plants.
newsitem.headline: Ericsson invests 1 bln Skr in Kista plants.

text.p: Swedish telecoms group Ericsson said on Friday it was investing around one billion crowns from 1996 to 1999 in its semi-conductor plants in Kista, just north of Stockholm.
"Over three to four years, from around 1996 to 1999, investments will total about one billion crowns," Bengt Callmer, head of information at Ericsson Components, told Reuters.
The company invested one billion crowns in a new semi-conductor plant in Kista in 1994 and Callmer said the company needs to keep investing in it.
"But we're increasing investments sharply now," he added.
"The main part of demand comes from the mobile phone market growth and from mobile phone systems but also from fixed line access devices," he said.
Currently, the plants produce 100,000 circuits a day.
"The investments will multiply capacity," Callmer said, declining to be more specific.
"It (how much capacity will increase) depends on how succesful we are in making good circuits," he said.
Callmer stressed that the investments reflected increased demand and that they would not stop Ericsson from buying semi-conductors from other manufacturers.
